subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the focus, vertex, equation of the directrix and the length of the latus rectum of the parabola y² − x + 4y + 5 = 0.

mark_split.label: Complete the square to reach the standard form
State the vertex, focus, directrix and latus rectum

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Complete the square
steps.margin_note: First mark, for correctly completing the square and reaching a = 1/4, h = 1, k = −2.
lines: This is a horizontal parabola opening in the +x direction. Comparing with (y − k)² = 4a(x − h) gives 4a = 1 ⇒ a = 1/4, h = 1, k = −2
steps.why: Completing the square on the y-terms is what turns this equation into the standard sideways form (y−k)² = 4a(x−h) — every one of the four quantities asked for reads straight off h, k and a once that form is reached.
common_mistakes: Completing the square with the wrong constant, adding 2 instead of 4 to both sides.
Reading off h and k with their signs swapped — the vertex is (h,k) = (1,−2), not (−1,2).
steps.memory_tip: Half of 4 is 2, and 2² = 4 — that is the number added to both sides to complete the square on y² + 4y.

steps.label: State the vertex, focus, directrix and latus rectum
steps.margin_note: Second mark, for all four answers together, each shifted from the origin case by h and k.
lines: (iii) Equation of the directrix: x = h − a ⇒ x = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4 ⇒ 4x − 3 = 0
steps.why: With the equation in standard form (y−k)² = 4a(x−h), the vertex is (h,k), the focus and directrix sit at h±a along the axis, and the latus rectum's length is always 4a — the same four facts as any sideways parabola, just centred at (h,k) instead of the origin.
common_mistakes: Adding a to h for the directrix instead of subtracting it (the directrix sits on the opposite side of the vertex from the focus).
Giving the latus rectum's length as a instead of 4a.
steps.memory_tip: Focus is h plus a; directrix is h minus a — the focus and directrix always sit on opposite sides of the vertex.

insider_note: This question is answer 127's method (vertex, focus, directrix, axis of a sideways parabola) with two extra twists — the equation must first be completed to standard form, and the vertex has shifted away from the origin.
